research.llm_analyst_verdict: The confluence of a bullish Sentinel bias, oversold RSI and price near the lower Bollinger Band points to a possible short‑term bounce, but watch the MACD for any bullish turn.

bull.thesis_summary: The case rests on three independent pillars: (1) Sentinel net bias of +10 (Long 22 vs Short 12) — a systematic signal with a documented edge in mean-reversion regimes; (2) RSI at 28.43, a genuine oversold extreme that has historically coincided with short-covering rallies in MARUTI when HV Rank is below 30 (currently 29); (3) FII 30-day net inflow of ₹280.1 Cr — real institutional accumulation, not a price-derived echo. MACD bearish and price below 200DMA are acknowledged headwinds; the thesis is a tactical oversold bounce, not a trend reversal. Friction cost is 0.2% of amount risked round-trip; ATR is ₹242.69. No Monte Carlo base rate was supplied, so the floor cannot be quantified — this trade is justified only if the oversold/flow confluence produces a move exceeding ~₹485 (2×ATR) within 5–10 sessions.

bear.thesis_summary: The trade fails because the "LOW_VOL regime" (VIX 11.15, 70% confidence) that underpins the mean-reversion edge is the exact condition where oversold bounces lack follow-through volume and fade into lower lows. RSI 28.43 is not a trigger — it is a symptom of persistent selling pressure that has already broken the 200DMA (price "Above 200DMA: None") and kept MACD bearish. The FII inflow (₹280.1 Cr) is a 30-day cumulative figure; it does not prove active buying *today* — it could be stale positioning from higher levels. In a LOW_VOL regime with no OI data, no dealer mode visibility, and PCR neutral (0.999), there is no derivatives confirmation that the selling is exhausted. The trade loses money when price churns sideways at oversold levels (ATR ₹242.69 implies ~₹485 range for 2×ATR) and time decay erodes the tactical thesis — the "3-session follow-through" exit rule becomes a death by a thousand cuts.
